Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Call recap:
- FinOpsCo is evaluating Redwood for inference workloads (chat + embeddings) across product and internal analytics.
- Procurement preference: AP typically requires a PO for new software vendors; payment by corporate card is limited to SaaS partners already onboarded.
- Interested in exploring both a standard commercial contract and Marketplace option if that shortens procurement.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share our vendor onboarding checklist so your AP/Procurement team can confirm data/financial info needed (attached).
2) Jenna — can you confirm whether FinOpsCo will accept invoice + PO (net30) or whether we should pursue a card pilot for initial proof-of-concept?
3) If PO is required, we’ll send PO instructions + draft SOW/invoice template for your legal/finance review.

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (vendor onboarding checklist — vendor profile, W-9, bank details, SOC2 evidence link)

If helpful I can also outline the marketplace option (AWS/GCP marketplace) which sometimes bypasses vendor onboarding for faster proof-of-value — happy to discuss.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple clarifications from procurement: 

- FinOpsCo policy: new vendors must be set up in our vendor system and paid via PO/invoice. We do not issue a corporate card payment to vendors we have not previously onboarded unless there is an approved one-time exception from Finance.
- Marketplace: We do use AWS Marketplace for some vendors. If Redwood is available on marketplace with metered billing, procurement can sometimes accept that path and skip the full vendor setup.

Next items on our side:
- I’ll confirm with AP what documentation they need (W-9, bank routing, standard terms).
- If we go PO route, can you send the PO instructions and an invoice/SOW template we can use to create the PO?

Also: timeline constraint — finance needs the vendor set up completed before end of month to align with our onboarding window.

Regards,

Subject: Internal: PO vs card - FinOpsCo (RDW-5421) - need guidance on payment exceptions / marketplace play

Lauren / Rishi — looping you in for quick guidance.

Context: FinOpsCo requires PO/invoice for new vendors and has a month-end onboarding window they want to hit. They asked for our PO instructions and invoice/SOW template. They also asked whether we have a marketplace presence that could accelerate start.

Questions: 
- Do we have an approved marketplace listing (AWS/GCP) for Redwood that would allow FinOpsCo to subscribe without vendor setup? If yes, who owns the marketplace listing?
- If marketplace not viable, what is the fastest path to accept PO (standard SOW + invoice) vs asking Finance for a one-time card exception for a short POC? What approvals would be required and how long?

Why this matters: If we can start via marketplace or a one-time card, we can kick off a POC this month which materially increases chance of expansion. If not, we should prioritize sending PO instructions and SOW template for AP to start vendor setup.

Deal: RDW-5421 (Sales opportunity; likely mid-market expansion).

Suggested immediate action: share PO_instructions.pdf and SOW_template.docx with Jenna; confirm whether legal needs to review the SOW or we can use standard terms.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer.

— Marissa
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PO vs card - FinOpsCo (RDW-5421) - next steps

Thanks for the thread and context, Marissa. Quick answers and recommended next steps: 

1) Marketplace — we have an AWS Marketplace listing in place for metered billing, but it currently covers only our hosted API SKUs (metered tokens). Marketplace team is cc'd internally (not on this thread) for billing enablement. If FinOpsCo is happy with that model it’s the fastest start. I'll follow up with the marketplace ops owner to confirm enrollment timeline (typically 1-2 weeks once legal/billing approvals are confirmed).

2) PO route — this is the standard. Please send the PO_instructions.pdf and SOW_template.docx to Jenna/AP so they can begin vendor setup. Legal has pre-approved our standard SOW template for mid-market customers; if they request changes we’ll route redlines but that will add time.

3) Card exception — Finance (Rishi) can consider a one-time card payment for a limited POC, but we need:
   - Approval from Finance (Rishi) + Sales Ops (me)
   - A closed plan for scope & spend cap (e.g., $5k cap, end date)
   - A short internal sign-off (24-48 hrs) if needed for deal acceleration

Action items for Marissa: 
- Send PO_instructions.pdf and SOW_template.docx to Jenna (copied below).
- Ask FinOpsCo to provide the W-9 and vendor bank details; confirm whether they can accept marketplace metered billing.
- If they request a card pilot, propose a clear POC scope and a spend cap and we’ll route to Finance.

I’ve attached PO_instructions.pdf and SOW_template.docx for your use. Also here is a DocuSign link for quick signature if they prefer to sign now: https://www.docusign.com/transactions/abcdef123456
